findings: aws:ResourceTag/ScopeProbe authorization uses live base-function tags for all four requested scopes: unqualified, explicit $LATEST, numeric version 1 and alias live. This was independently observed for InvokeFunction, GetFunction and GetFunctionConfiguration; GetAlias(live) follows the same live base-tag behavior.

Before changing the base tag, three complete 13-cell matrices each showed unconditional and ScopeProbe=before sessions succeeding everywhere, with ScopeProbe=after and Null:true sessions denied everywhere. All 13 unconditional positive-control cells also succeeded before the conditional matrices began.

After publication and alias creation, changing only the base ScopeProbe tag from before to after reversed both StringEquals sessions in every cell: the old-value session denied and the new-value session succeeded. Four repeated post-change matrices over a 77.881-second bounded observation window retained the same result, while unconditional requests succeeded throughout. Published numeric and alias authorization therefore did not use frozen publication-time tag snapshots.

The Null:true tag session denied every tested cell in all seven conditional matrices. Its denial alone would not establish context presence, but the matching StringEquals successes and their reversal after the live tag change independently establish a present, current tag context rather than absent qualified context.

The 116 synchronous RequestResponse Invoke requests produced 60 successful real runtime responses and 56 AccessDeniedException results. Every successful response had HTTP/application status 200 without FunctionError, echoed its unique input marker, and reported the expected executed version: $LATEST for unqualified/explicit $LATEST and 1 for numeric/alias requests.

The fixture retains 419 native observations, immutable session policies and actor identities, deterministic ZIP bytes/source/hash, native error and success bodies, request IDs, decoded runtime payloads and eight matrix summaries. No simulator or DryRun response is used as invocation authority evidence.

Cleanup deleted the owned alias, numeric version, base function, caller inline policy and both IAM roles. Explicit native readbacks confirmed all absent, including the log group; the execution role had no log permissions and deleting its never-created log group returned ResourceNotFoundException.
limitations: Observations cover this account/region and identity/session-policy authorization for aws:ResourceTag/ScopeProbe on Invoke, GetFunction, GetFunctionConfiguration and GetAlias. They do not establish behavior for other APIs or organization policies.
No IAM simulator or DryRun observations substitute for runtime Invoke responses. No resource-based Lambda policy was installed.

Tag propagation is bounded by the recorded repeated matrices, not assumed instantaneous. There was no observed stale-tag authorization in these post-change matrices, but this does not establish a universal propagation-time bound.

The Null:true condition was a negative control while the base tag existed; this experiment did not remove the base tag to obtain a positive missing-tag control. Presence is established by the successful matching StringEquals controls, not by Null denial alone.
